scope: Offline analysis of current FP16 Instruments capture with supplied same-run device comparison report. Shader samples identify expensive families, not exact MIL operations.
method: Resolve XML id/ref independently per document. Match Core ML Prediction spans by model; filter GPU Active and shader rows to PID 7849. Clip to each prediction, union overlaps, and exclude the first prediction of each model. Family groups remove trailing numeric shader ID only. SDPA group is shader names containing sdpa. Shader/GPU/prediction intervals overlap and are not additive.
interpretation: Warm propagation median 33.824 ms; GPU Active union median 28.414 ms; all sampled SDPA intervals union median 15.932 ms. Attention is the largest observed shader family group.

Encoder median 22.791 ms; GPU Active union 21.212 ms. Largest sampled encoder family is mmul_kernel_a16_float_float_float, 4.627 ms median; shader name alone cannot establish exact MIL operation or safe precision change.

limitations: Shader samples cover part of GPU-active time; gaps are not necessarily idle time. Family medians need not sum to group medians.

Accuracy and fixture identity are provided by the associated temporal report, not timing XML. All reported numerical/input/state fields equal the bulk-copy baseline; this does not prove tensor byte identity or annotated ground-truth accuracy.
